approachQuestion.prompt: Process at most 200,000 immutable commands ENQUEUE(x) and DEQUEUE; DEQUEUE is never called when empty. Return dequeued values in order. Values are fixed-size integers. Example [ENQUEUE(4),ENQUEUE(9),DEQUEUE,ENQUEUE(2),DEQUEUE,DEQUEUE] -> [4,9,2].

options.text: Push enqueued values onto input stack. On DEQUEUE, if output stack is empty transfer all input values to it, then pop output.
options.feedback: After ENQUEUE(4) and ENQUEUE(9), transferring into empty output puts 4 above 9. Pop 4 first. A later ENQUEUE(2) stays in input until the older output value 9 is removed, preserving FIFO order.

options.text: Keep a circular array queue with head and tail indices, advancing indices on enqueue/dequeue.
options.feedback: A circular array is equally optimal when capacity is managed without copying; both are correct alternatives.

options.text: Use one array queue and shift remaining values left after every dequeue.
options.feedback: Shifting is correct but repeated movement makes a long drain costly.

options.text: Before every dequeue, transfer all input values onto output even if output still contains older queued values.
options.feedback: For ENQUEUE(4), ENQUEUE(9), DEQUEUE, ENQUEUE(2), DEQUEUE, the second transfer puts 2 above 9 and returns 2 instead of 9.

feedback.reason: Transfer only when output is empty: reversing input then puts the oldest queued value on top.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For two-stack-fifo-amortization-optimal, let n be the number of input commands or tokens. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Input is immutable; output storage is excluded.
constraints: Use a dynamically sized array for each stack; push/pop are worst-case constant time in this model.
For the two-stack method, each enqueued item transfers from input to output at most once over the full command sequence. Analyze total sequence time (amortized per command).
Input is immutable and returned output storage is excluded; both working stacks count. No whole-array copying occurs.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each value transfers at most once across the entire command sequence.
details: Across n commands, each value is pushed onto input once, transferred to output at most once, and popped at most once. Thus total time is O(n), or O(1) amortized per command; a single dequeue can still trigger a linear transfer. n enqueues without dequeues retain n values in the two working stacks, so auxiliary space is O(n).
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: n enqueues can leave n values across the two working stacks. Output exclusion does not exclude these stored queued values.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each value enters input once, transfers to output at most once, and leaves output once. One expensive transfer does not imply quadratic total work.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A sequence of n commands requires n command inspections even when no transfer is necessary.
